summary.headline: Wipro Q4 FY26 IT Services revenue flat QoQ at $2.65B (+0.2% cc), Q1 FY27 guided -2% to 0% QoQ cc, with a INR15,000 crore buyback approved.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 IT Services revenue was $2.65B, up 0.2% sequentially and down 0.2% YoY in constant currency, with FY26 revenue down 1.6%. Operating margin was 17.3% (down 30 bps QoQ) and FY26 margin was 17.2% (up about 15 bps). Order bookings were $3.5B (up 3.2% QoQ, down 13.9% YoY) including 14 large deals worth $1.4B. Americas 2 (BFSI-led) fell sharply on a client-specific issue and a delayed large-deal ramp-up, while Americas 1, Europe and APMEA grew sequentially. The board approved a INR15,000 crore buyback at INR250 per share, the largest in Wipro's history.

segments.name: Americas 1
segments.commentary: Grew 0.3% QoQ and 2.9% YoY cc in Q4, driven by consumer, technology and communications; healthcare hit by seasonality and policy changes.

segments.name: Americas 2
segments.commentary: Declined 2.6% QoQ and 6.7% YoY cc, mainly BFSI, due to delayed ramp-ups on large deals and a client-specific issue.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 IT Services revenue guided to -2% to 0% QoQ cc, equal to $2.597B to $2.651B.

Two strategic deals announced in April (including Olam and a vendor-consolidation win) are included in guidance, assumed to contribute for about 1.5 months at mid-quarter; management estimated roughly 0.7-0.8% of revenue from them, per an analyst's calculation.
DTS HARMAN adds about one incremental month in Q1 (analyst estimate about 0.7-0.8% of revenue). Management said Q4 already included all three months.
Q1 margin headwinds: two months of wage hike effective 1 March, lower initial margins on large competitive deals, and HARMAN connected services; quarterly volatility expected.
Medium-term aim is to keep operating margin within a narrow band through productivity, cost takeout, AI-enabled fixed-price delivery and overhead optimisation.
Buyback of INR15,000 crore at INR250 per share (about 5.7% of paid-up capital), expected to complete in Q1 FY27 subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Investment to continue in the new AI-native business and platforms unit (services-as-a-software model), with investment details to be shared once strategy is formed.
Wipro Intelligence platform launched two quarters earlier; industry platforms in healthcare, banking, insurance and telecom; delivery platforms WINGS (run and operate) and WEGA (SDLC).
Larger deals may bring some balance-sheet leverage (higher unbilled/working capital) but management said this is business as usual.
Capability investments include DTS HARMAN connected services, which is pressuring margins.
demand_pricing: Management said IT spending has shown resilience despite geopolitical and policy disruption; cloud, data and AI investments continue, with spending increasingly tied to outcomes.
Pipeline described as strong and secular across industries and markets; competitive intensity is high, and large deals are being won in competitive environments with lower initial margins.
Americas 2 BFSI weakness was described as client-specific (client changed strategy and paused) and not a broader trend; management said no clients were showing specific geopolitical behaviour.
Manufacturing and auto clients are watching and waiting amid tariffs and input-cost pressure, tightening budgets but not changing strategy.
Top account revenue fell sequentially but was up YoY; top 5 clients grew 0.2% YoY cc and top 10 grew 1.5% YoY cc in Q4.
Unbilled revenue rose by more than $80M in the quarter; management called it a quarterly aberration, with DSO flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why have large-deal ramp-ups been delayed repeatedly, and does Q1 guidance reflect that?
qa_highlights.answer: Srini Pallia said the Americas 2 BFSI softness was a mix of a client-specific issue and a delayed ramp-up; the client changed strategy, the issue ends in Q1 with no material impact after, and visibility is good on timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the top client's revenue down sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Aparna Iyer called it a one-off quarterly volatility on a long-standing healthy relationship; top 5 clients grew 0.2% YoY and top 10 grew 1.5% YoY in cc.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unbilled revenue rise by over $80M, and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Aparna Iyer said it is a quarterly aberration expected to correct; DSO flat YoY, operating cash flow 112% of net income, and long-term unbilled contained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 organic growth implied after the two new deals and HARMAN?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two deals and one extra HARMAN month add inorganic-like contribution; the new deals are strategic, not inorganic, and included in the guided range. HARMAN Q4 revenue was implied as a quarterly run-rate by the filing.

qa_highlights.question: Are the current margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Aparna Iyer said wage hikes, lower-margin large deals, HARMAN and investment in Wipro Intelligence will pressure margins; the goal is to hold margins in a narrow band over the medium term with some quarterly volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Americas 2 client weakness recurring, and how is Wipro engaging on AI partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Srini Pallia said the two Q4 and Q1 issues were specific; Wipro is pivoting to AI-native platforms and services-as-a-software and sees clients asking for AI advisory, with Wipro Intelligence and platform traction in healthcare, banking, insurance and telecom.

risks_watch: Americas 2 BFSI: whether the delayed ramp-up and client-specific issue end in Q1 as management said; Q1 guidance relies on this.
Q1 guidance dependence on two newly won deals (mid-quarter start) and HARMAN's extra month; organic growth implied is weak.
Margin pressure from two months of wage hikes, lower-margin large deals and investment in AI platforms; margin band may widen.
Order bookings down 13.9% YoY in Q4, and a competitive environment for large deals.
Unbilled revenue increase of over $80M; watch whether it reverses next quarter and whether larger deals add balance-sheet leverage.
Buyback execution (INR15,000 crore) subject to shareholder approval and timing in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on pipeline, AI strategy and capital returns, but defensive and repeatedly vague on the Americas 2 BFSI slump and on the cause of repeated ramp-up delays. Management also declined to quantify organic growth in Q1 guidance.
key_quotes: Three out of the 4 SMUs, Americas, as well as Europe and APMEA have grown sequentially.
we are making a deliberate strategic pivot to stay ahead.
we expect to buy back 5.7% of the paid-up capital.
we will have the headwinds of two months of salary increase and a few large deals that we've won, and the volatility could be there in our quarterly performance.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 IT Services revenue guided to -2% to 0% QoQ cc (midpoint about -1%), backed by $3.5B Q4 bookings (14 large deals, $1.4B) and two April deals (Olam, vendor consolidation) included in guidance, though no capacity additions were cited.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 operating margin fell 30 bps QoQ to 17.3%, and Q1 faces two months of wage hikes, lower initial margins on large competitive deals and HARMAN connected services; management only targets a 'narrow band' medium term.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY27 guided -2% to 0% QoQ cc ($2.597B to $2.651B), with the midpoint near -1%; Q4 bookings were $3.5B (+3.2% QoQ, -13.9% YoY) and Americas 2 is expected to stabilise in Q1, but the guide relies on two April deals and an extra HARMAN month.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Investment continues in the AI-native services-as-a-software unit and Wipro Intelligence, with details to come once strategy is formed; no utilisation figure was given to test capacity need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 guide is -2% to 0% QoQ cc with a midpoint near -1%, and management declined to quantify organic growth; the guide depends on newly won deals and an extra HARMAN month.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 guidance depends on Americas 2 BFSI issues ending in Q1 and on two mid-quarter deals (about 0.7-0.8% of revenue each per the analyst estimate), and Americas 2 fell 2.6% QoQ in Q4; margin headwinds also persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wipro Intelligence platform launched two quarters ago, with industry platforms in healthcare, banking, insurance and telecom and delivery platforms WINGS and WEGA already named; further platform rollouts are implied but no dates were given.

rows.label: INR15,000 crore buyback at INR250/share
rows.why: Board approved buyback of about 5.7% of paid-up capital, expected to complete in Q1 FY27 subject to shareholder approval; FY26 payout ratio about 88% vs 70% policy minimum.

rows.label: Large-deal conversion and Americas 2 recovery
rows.why: Q4 bookings were $3.5B with 14 large deals worth $1.4B and Olam deal over $1B TCV ($800M committed spend), but Americas 2 fell 6.7% YoY cc on a delayed ramp-up and client-specific issue that management says ends in Q1.

rows.label: Unbilled revenue normalisation
rows.why: Unbilled revenue rose by more than $80M in Q4, which management called a quarterly aberration expected to correct; DSO flat YoY and operating cash flow 112.6% of net income.

tone.note: Management was confident on pipeline, AI platforms and capital returns, but was defensive and vague on the Americas 2 BFSI slump, repeated ramp-up delays and organic growth in Q1 guidance; analysts pressed on the sustainability of margins.
